les: Siektes wat van mens tot mens oorgaan
kaps_punt: Oordraagbare siektes soos pampoentjies, tuberkulose, verkoue, waterpokkies, atleetvoet, ensovoorts. Oorsake van oordraagbare siektes; Tekens en simptome van oordraagbare siektes; Waar om inligting te vind: Voorkomingstrategieë; en Beskikbare behandeling.

items.bewering: 'n Siekte wat van een mens of dier na 'n ander kan oorgaan, is oordraagbaar.
items.bron: Standard definition of a communicable disease: 'transmitted from one person or animal to another'; the broader IAEA formulation adds inanimate sources and vectors, which the lesson does not exclude (https://dictionary.dogonews.com/definitions/communicable%20disease ; https://www-pub.iaea.org/MTCD/Meetings/PDFplus/2007/cn159/cn159_Mas-Coma.pdf). Volledige check, eerste ronde.

items.bewering: Die meeste oordraagbare siektes kom van baie klein dinge, soos kieme.
items.bron: Germs (microscopic bacteria, viruses, fungi and protozoa) cause infectious disease (KidsHealth, https://kidshealth.org/en/parents/germs.html). 'Die meeste' is safe and, if anything, cautious: the exceptions are larger parasites such as worms.

items.bewering: Atleetvoet kom van 'n swam. Hierdie swam is ook 'n kiem, want dit is 'n baie klein lewende ding wat jou siek kan maak.
items.bron: NHS: 'Athlete's foot is a common fungal infection' (https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/athletes-foot/). KidsHealth counts fungi among germs and names athlete's foot (https://kidshealth.org/en/teens/care-about-germs.html). The fungi that cause it are microscopic (EBSCO Research Starters, https://www.ebsco.com/research-starters/health-and-medicine/athletes-foot).

items.bewering: Druppeltjies met hierdie klein dinge spat in die lug wanneer 'n siek mens hoes of nies. Hulle kan ook op hande en gedeelde dinge sit.
items.blok: Hoe siektes oorgaan en hoe hulle wys
items.bron: CDC common cold: most respiratory viruses spread through droplets from coughs or sneezes, and by touching a contaminated surface (https://www.cdc.gov/common-cold/about/index.html). NHS: germs from coughs and sneezes 'can live on hands and surfaces for 24 hours' (https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/common-cold/).

items.bewering: Party kieme leef op nat vloere waar mense kaalvoet loop.
items.blok: Hoe siektes oorgaan en hoe hulle wys
items.bron: NHS: athlete's foot spreads by 'walking barefoot in places where someone else has athlete's foot – especially changing rooms and showers' (https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/athletes-foot/). Damp pool and locker-room floors are a common route (EBSCO, https://www.ebsco.com/research-starters/health-and-medicine/athletes-foot).

items.bewering: Pyn en moegheid is simptome. Die siek mens ervaar hulle self. Koors en 'n uitslag is tekens. 'n Ander mens kan hulle self sien of meet, ook al vertel die siek mens niks.
items.blok: Hoe siektes oorgaan en hoe hulle wys
items.bron: Symptoms are subjective and felt only by the patient; signs are objective and can be observed or measured by others. Fever and rash are given as signs, pain and fatigue as symptoms (EBSCO Research Starters, https://www.ebsco.com/research-starters/health-and-medicine/understanding-disease-signs-and-symptoms ; GoodRx, https://www.goodrx.com/health-topic/diagnostics/signs-vs-symptoms). Nuance, not an error: a rash the patient notices is also a symptom. The lesson says only that a rash is a sign, not that it is never a symptom.

items.bewering: Pampoentjies kom van 'n virus wat deur druppeltjies en speeksel oorgaan as iemand hoes, nies of 'n beker deel.
items.bron: CDC: mumps is 'caused by a virus'; it 'spreads through direct contact with saliva or respiratory droplets', including by coughing and sneezing and through shared 'water bottles or cups' (https://www.cdc.gov/mumps/about/index.html).

items.bewering: 'n Pynlike swelling verskyn gewoonlik onder en voor die oor langs die kakebeen aan een of albei kante.
items.bron: CDC: 'swollen salivary glands under one or both ears' and 'painful swelling of the jaw' (https://www.cdc.gov/mumps/about/index.html). The parotid glands sit at the angle of the jaw, in front of and below the ear (Mediktor, https://my.mediktor.com/en/disease/mumps-parotitis). NHS: swelling usually on one or both sides, and some people have none, so 'gewoonlik' is correct (https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/mumps/).

items.bewering: Dikwels het die kind koors en hoofpyn, en is dit pynlik om te kou of te sluk.
items.bron: NHS: high temperature and headache; mumps may 'make it harder to chew, swallow or speak' (https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/mumps/). CDC lists fever and headache as common (https://www.cdc.gov/mumps/about/index.html).

items.bewering: Tuberkulose (TB) kom van kieme wat meestal in die longe groei.
items.bron: WHO: TB is 'caused by bacteria that most often affects the lungs' (https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/tuberculosis). CDC: caused by 'a bacterium (or germ)', and 'TB usually affects the lungs' (https://www.cdc.gov/tb/about/index.html).

items.bewering: Die kieme gaan deur die lug oor as iemand met TB hoes, nie deur 'n gedeelde beker, bord of kos nie.
items.bron: CDC: 'TB is spread through the air from one person to another' when someone with active lung TB coughs, speaks or sings (https://www.cdc.gov/tb/about/index.html). New York State DOH: TB is not spread by sharing cups or cutlery (https://health.ny.gov/diseases/communicable/tuberculosis/docs/fact_sheet.pdf). CDC's older wording lists 'sharing food or drink' among things that do not spread TB. Speaking and singing also spread it. The lesson does not say coughing is the only way, so this is not an error.

items.bewering: Die belangrikste waarskuwing is 'n hoes wat twee weke of langer aanhou.
items.bron: The South African threshold is two weeks: the Western Cape Government TB Control Programme gives 'coughing for more than 2 weeks' as the first main sign (https://d7.westerncape.gov.za/service/tb-control-programme). Arrive Alive: anyone with a cough of 'two weeks or more' must be tested, free at any clinic (https://www.arrivealive.co.za/print.aspx?i=941). WHO lists 'prolonged cough' first (https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/tuberculosis). The US CDC uses three weeks, but the lesson rightly follows the South African standard. In people living with HIV a cough of any length counts. 'Belangrikste' is not 'enigste', so it holds.

items.bewering: Iemand met TB kan ook koors hê, snags sweet, baie moeg word en gewig verloor.
items.bron: WHO lists fever, night sweats, weight loss and fatigue (https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/tuberculosis). CDC: fever, night sweats, weight loss, weakness or fatigue (https://www.cdc.gov/tb/about/index.html).

items.bewering: Nie elke hoes is TB nie. Gaan wel met so 'n lang hoes kliniek toe. Gaan vroeër as jy bekommerd is.
items.bron: A cough is a main symptom of a common cold (NHS, https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/common-cold/). A South African cough of two weeks or more should be tested, free at any clinic (Arrive Alive, https://www.arrivealive.co.za/print.aspx?i=941).

items.bewering: 'n Verkoue kom van een van baie verskillende virusse.
items.bron: CDC: 'More than 200 respiratory viruses can cause colds' (https://www.cdc.gov/common-cold/about/index.html).

items.bewering: Dit gaan oor deur druppeltjies en hande wat die virus na jou neus of mond dra.
items.bron: CDC: it spreads by droplets, or by touching a contaminated surface and then your 'eyes, nose, or mouth' (https://www.cdc.gov/common-cold/about/index.html). Leaving out the eyes does not make the claim false.

items.bewering: Jy kan nies en ook 'n loopneus of toe neus, keelseer en 'n hoes kry.
items.bron: NHS: a blocked or runny nose, sneezing, sore throat and cough are the main symptoms (https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/common-cold/). CDC lists the same (https://www.cdc.gov/common-cold/about/index.html).

items.bewering: Koue weer of nat hare alleen gee jou nie 'n verkoue nie.
items.bron: Colds are caused by viruses, so wet hair cannot give you one (The Naked Scientists, https://www.thenakedscientists.com/articles/interviews/will-wet-hair-give-you-cold ; THIP fact check, https://www.thip.media/health-news-fact-check/fact-check-will-wet-hair-make-you-catch-a-cold/22121/). CDC: you can get a cold any time of year (https://www.cdc.gov/common-cold/about/index.html). A 2005 Cardiff study found that chilling can slightly raise symptoms in people already carrying a virus. The word 'alleen' covers this exactly.

items.bewering: Waterpokkies kom ook van 'n virus. Dit gaan baie maklik oor deur die lug en wanneer iemand aan die blasies raak.
items.bron: CDC: 'highly contagious disease caused by the varicella-zoster virus'; up to 90% of non-immune close contacts become infected (https://www.cdc.gov/chickenpox/about/index.html). Rhode Island DOH and HealthLinkBC: it spreads through the air when an infected person coughs or sneezes, and through contact with blister fluid (https://health.ri.gov/infectious-diseases/varicella-chickenpox ; https://www.healthlinkbc.ca/healthwise/chickenpox-varicella).

items.bewering: Die kind kry 'n jeukerige uitslag van kolle en dikwels koors en moegheid. Die kolle word blasies wat tot korsies opdroog.
items.bron: NHS: 'an itchy, spotty rash'; the spots fill with fluid and become blisters, then form a scab; also high temperature (https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/chickenpox/). CDC: rash turns into itchy fluid-filled blisters that turn into scabs (https://www.cdc.gov/chickenpox/about/index.html). Fever and tiredness are common early symptoms (Rhode Island DOH, https://health.ri.gov/infectious-diseases/varicella-chickenpox).

items.bewering: Moenie krap nie.
items.bron: NHS: 'Do not scratch the spots, as scratching can cause scarring' (https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/chickenpox/).

items.bewering: Die swam van atleetvoet groei in warm en nat plekke soos tussen sweterige tone. Dit gaan oor op nat vloere van storte en kleedkamers en deur gedeelde handdoeke of skoene.
items.bron: NHS: spreads in changing rooms and showers; more likely with wet or sweaty feet; do not share towels, socks or shoes (https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/athletes-foot/). The fungi thrive in warm, moist places, and damp locker-room and pool floors and shared towels are routes of spread (EBSCO, https://www.ebsco.com/research-starters/health-and-medicine/athletes-foot ; Northwestern Medicine, https://www.nm.org/conditions-and-care-areas/dermatology/athletes-foot/causes-and-diagnoses).

items.bewering: Die vel tussen die tone kan jeuk, wit en klam lyk en afskilfer of kraak.
items.bron: NHS: 'itchy white patches between your toes', 'sore and flaky patches', skin 'may become cracked' (https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/athletes-foot/). EBSCO: white peeling skin between the toes, in a moist setting (https://www.ebsco.com/research-starters/health-and-medicine/athletes-foot).

items.bewering: Hoes en nies in jou elmboog of 'n snesie. Was jou hande dikwels met seep en water. Moenie bekers, handdoeke of skoene deel nie. Laat vars lug in en bly by die huis as jy siek is. Droog jou voete goed af tussen die tone en dra plakkies in 'n gedeelde stort.
items.bron: Public health guidance is to use a tissue or your elbow, wash hands with soap and water, and stay home when sick (Louisiana DOH, https://ldh.la.gov/assets/oph/LDH_KeepIllnessFromSpreading_.pdf ; NHS cold, https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/common-cold/). Do not share cups: mumps spreads through shared cups (CDC, https://www.cdc.gov/mumps/about/index.html). Do not share towels or shoes; dry between the toes; wear flip-flops in showers (NHS, https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/athletes-foot/). Fresh air: ventilation cuts airborne TB risk in South African clinics (UCT, https://open.uct.ac.za/items/4e47ad3c-6737-4ecb-b8c2-cbf7c8af09e4/full ; CDC TB, https://www.cdc.gov/tb/about/index.html). The advice not to share cups does not clash with the TB block, which only says TB does not spread that way.

items.bewering: Die kliniek sê watter behandeling nodig is. Vir party siektes is dit medisyne. TB kan gesond gemaak word.
items.bron: WHO: 'Tuberculosis is preventable and curable' (https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/tuberculosis). CDC: active TB 'can be treated with medicine' (https://www.cdc.gov/tb/about/index.html).

items.bewering: Om die medisyne klaar te drink, gee die beste kans om gesond te word.
items.bron: CDC: 'You will need to take and finish all of your TB medicine as directed' (https://www.cdc.gov/tb/about/index.html). EWN 2026: poor treatment adherence is driving ongoing TB transmission in South Africa (https://www.ewn.co.za/2026/04/29/persistent-cough-could-signal-tb-health-experts-warn). 'Medisyne drink' for tablets is ordinary Afrikaans usage and was not judged as a fact.

items.bewering: Vir 'n verkoue is dit gewoonlik rus en baie drink. Gaan wel kliniek toe as 'n verkoue nie beter word nie en dadelik as asemhaal moeilik word.
items.bron: NHS: 'plenty of rest', drink 'lots of fluid'; see a GP if symptoms do not get better after 10 days or you feel short of breath (https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/common-cold/). Seattle Children's: trouble breathing means seeing a doctor right away, or calling emergency services if severe (https://www.seattlechildrens.org/conditions/a-z/colds/).

items.bewering: Vertel 'n grootmens as jy siek voel. Of julle saam kliniek toe gaan, hang van die siekte af.
items.bron: This is consistent with the guidance above: most colds are treated at home (NHS, https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/common-cold/), while a cough lasting two weeks should be tested at a clinic (Arrive Alive, https://www.arrivealive.co.za/print.aspx?i=941). It is advice, with no factual content beyond that.

items.bewering: Vra 'n verpleegster, 'n dokter of iemand by jou skool. Lees die kliniek se plakkate en pamflette. Nie alles wat mense sê of wat aanlyn staan, is waar nie. As jy twyfel, vra by die kliniek.
items.bron: The wet-hair myth is a widely circulated false health claim, rated false by fact-checkers (THIP, https://www.thip.media/health-news-fact-check/fact-check-will-wet-hair-make-you-catch-a-cold/22121/). South African public clinics offer free TB testing and health services (Arrive Alive, https://www.arrivealive.co.za/print.aspx?i=941 ; GCIS pocket guide, https://www.gcis.gov.za/sites/default/files/docs/resourcecentre/pocketguide/2004/health04.pdf). It is advice, with no other checkable claim.

items.bewering: oordraagbaar: Gesê van 'n siekte wat van een mens of dier na 'n ander kan oorgaan.
items.bron: Checked alone and in its block. It matches the dictionary definition 'any disease transmitted from one person or animal to another' (https://dictionary.dogonews.com/definitions/communicable%20disease). It also agrees word for word with the first study block.

items.bewering: kieme: Baie klein lewende dinge wat 'n mens siek kan maak.
items.bron: Checked alone and in its block. It is true of bacteria, fungi and protozoa (KidsHealth, https://kidshealth.org/en/parents/germs.html). For a person to know, not an error: in everyday English 'germs' includes viruses, and whether viruses are alive is debated (Ankara University course notes, https://acikders.ankara.edu.tr/mod/resource/view.php?id=139689). The lesson never calls a virus a 'kiem' or a living thing. It says the cold, mumps and chickenpox come from 'n virus', and the virus entry says only 'ding'. So no sentence in it states that a virus is alive.

items.bewering: virus: 'n Baie klein ding wat net binne-in 'n liggaam skade kan doen.
items.bron: Checked alone and in its block. Viruses multiply only inside living host cells and are inert outside them (UC Berkeley UCMP, https://ucmp.berkeley.edu/alllife/virus.html ; Wikipedia, viral life cycle, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viral_life_cycle). KidsHealth: viruses 'can't survive unless they're living inside something else (such as a person, animal, or plant)' (https://kidshealth.org/en/parents/germs.html). 'Liggaam' simplifies 'host cell' without becoming false. In its block it does not clash with spread by hands: the entry is about doing harm, not about being carried.

items.bewering: swam: 'n Lewende ding soos skimmel of 'n sampioen; party swamme is te klein om te sien en kan 'n mens siek maak.
items.bron: Checked alone and in its block. Fungi include moulds and mushrooms, and the fungi that cause athlete's foot are microscopic (EBSCO, https://www.ebsco.com/research-starters/health-and-medicine/athletes-foot ; KidsHealth, https://kidshealth.org/en/teens/care-about-germs.html). The example also holds as a comparison: the entry says outright that some are too small to see, so a learner does not picture a visible mushroom on the foot.

items.bewering: simptoom: Iets wat wys dat 'n mens se gesondheid skeefloop en wat hy self ervaar, soos pyn, moegheid of naarheid.
items.bron: Checked alone and in its block. Symptoms are subjective and perceived only by the person; nausea, pain and fatigue are standard examples (EBSCO, https://www.ebsco.com/research-starters/health-and-medicine/understanding-disease-signs-and-symptoms ; GoodRx, https://www.goodrx.com/health-topic/diagnostics/signs-vs-symptoms).

items.bewering: teken: Iets wat wys dat 'n mens se gesondheid skeefloop en wat 'n ander mens self kan sien, hoor, ruik of meet, ook al vertel hy niks, soos 'n uitslag of koors.
items.bron: Checked alone and in its block. A sign is objective: something others can observe or measure, including with instruments. Fever and rash are standard examples (EBSCO, https://www.ebsco.com/research-starters/health-and-medicine/understanding-disease-signs-and-symptoms ; GoodRx, https://www.goodrx.com/health-topic/diagnostics/signs-vs-symptoms). It is consistent with the study block.

items.bewering: pampoentjies: 'n Siekte wat deur 'n virus veroorsaak word, gewoonlik met 'n pynlike swelling onder en voor die oor aan een of albei kante.
items.bron: Checked alone and in its block. CDC: caused by a virus; salivary glands swell under one or both ears (https://www.cdc.gov/mumps/about/index.html). The parotid gland lies in front of and below the ear (Mediktor, https://my.mediktor.com/en/disease/mumps-parotitis).

items.bewering: tuberkulose: 'n Siekte wat deur kieme veroorsaak word, meestal in 'n mens se longe.
items.bron: Checked alone and in its block. WHO: caused by bacteria, most often affects the lungs; it can also affect kidneys, brain and spine, which 'meestal' allows (https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/tuberculosis).

items.bewering: waterpokkies: 'n Siekte wat deur 'n virus veroorsaak word, met 'n jeukerige uitslag van blasies.
items.bron: Checked alone and in its block. CDC: caused by the varicella-zoster virus; the rash turns into itchy fluid-filled blisters (https://www.cdc.gov/chickenpox/about/index.html).

items.bewering: atleetvoet: 'n Siekte wat deur 'n swam veroorsaak word, met jeukerige vel tussen die tone.
items.bron: Checked alone and in its block. NHS: a fungal infection with 'itchy white patches between your toes' (https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/athletes-foot/).

items.bewering: kliniek: 'n Plek in die gemeenskap waar mense gesondheidsorg kry, of hulle siek is of gesond.
items.bron: Checked alone and in its block. South African primary health care clinics provide immunisation, family planning, antenatal care and child screening, which are services for healthy people as well as care for the sick (GCIS pocket guide, https://www.gcis.gov.za/sites/default/files/docs/resourcecentre/pocketguide/2004/health04.pdf ; Bluff PHC clinic, https://citizen.co.za/southlands-sun/news-headlines/2019/02/26/bluff-phc-clinic-services/amp).

items.bewering: medisyne: 'n Middel wat help om siekte of pyn te behandel, of om te keer dat 'n mens siek word.
items.bron: Checked alone and in its block. Medicine treats disease, and some prevents it. CDC: treating inactive TB with medicine 'is the best way to protect against becoming sick with active TB disease' (https://www.cdc.gov/tb/about/index.html).

items.bewering: Titel: Siektes wat van mens tot mens oorgaan
items.bron: All five diseases named pass from person to person. Mumps, the cold and chickenpox: CDC pages above. TB: CDC, 'from one person to another'. Athlete's foot: by direct contact or through shared floors (NHS, https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/athletes-foot/).

opsomming: All 42 claims, including every glossary entry read alone and in its block, are confirmed against health-authority sources (CDC, WHO, NHS, Western Cape Government): no analogy, no false claim, three superlatives that hold, and nothing uncertain; one point for a person, not an error: the lesson calls germs living things and never calls a virus a germ, so it says nothing about whether viruses are alive, and that should not be 'tidied' into a sentence that does.
